messages.subject: custom function in brewed file
messages.body_plain:
I have created custom function e.g. summ() (returns a data.frame) in
the file which is parsed by brew() function.
However, when i try to run the file, i receive error that summ()
function does not exist.
How can I add custom functions?

Sorry, if my question is trivial, but I am very beginner.
p.

messages.subject: Re: detecting RApache
messages.body_plain:
Excellent. Thank you. Do you know how to automatically detect the
correct path for this line, which has to be put into the Apache config
file? You just wrote /apache/module/path/ in the help file.

LoadModule R_module     /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so

On Oct 7, 7:49 pm, Jeffrey Horner <jeffrey.hor...@vanderbilt.edu>
wrote:

> Yes. Depending on how apache was packaged you can either call the
> apache binary or apachectl shell script with the -M argument and grep
> for R_module. For instance on Ubuntu (my machine):
>
> $ apache2ctl -M 2>&1 | grep R_module
>  R_module (shared)
>
> reveals that indeed rApache is installed.
>
> Jeff
>
> On Thu, Oct 7, 2010 at 6:40 PM, Brad Friedman
>
>
>
> <brad.aaron.fried...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > I am trying to write an install script for a software package that
> > depends on RApache. Is there a way I can automatically detect whether
> > or not RApache is already installed on the machine?
>
> > Thank you,
>
> > Brad Friedman

messages.subject: Re: detecting RApache
messages.body_plain:
On Thu, Nov 4, 2010 at 2:13 PM, Brad Friedman
<brad.aaro...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Excellent. Thank you. Do you know how to automatically detect the
> correct path for this line, which has to be put into the Apache config
> file? You just wrote /apache/module/path/ in the help file.
>
> LoadModule R_module     /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so

I think this will tell you reliably:

$ apxs2 -q LIBEXECDIR
/usr/lib/apache2/modules

So you could build a command like so:

$ echo "LoadModule R_module `apxs2 -q LIBEXECDIR`/mod_R.so"

Jeff
